**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The IP/data allocation in this in-licence runs in our favour on every material term of the rule:

- **We own what we create.** §11.1(a) (p0557) vests title to all IP made solely by Ono personnel in Ono; §4.6(c) (p0329) confirms Ono owns its INDs and Marketing Approvals in the Ono Territory; §2.7 (p0198) preserves retained rights with no implied grants. Array's ownership of its own compound/platform IP under §11.1(b) is expressly acceptable under the rule.
- **Licence-back is satisfied and then some.** §13.1 (p0627) converts our Article II licences on expiry into non-exclusive, fully paid-up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licences with sublicensing rights for the Ono Territory — the fallback position, reached by contract.
- **No assignment of our IP or data to the counterparty during the term.** The §2.6 Grant-Back (p0197) is non-exclusive, royalty-free and expressly "subject to the exclusive rights granted to Ono", i.e. a licence, not an assignment.

Two items sit at the fallback and are noted in the rationale rather than flagged:

1. **Joint ownership** is created by §11.1(c), and §11.1(d) restricts each Party to internal practice absent consent — but the restriction is reciprocal and disapplied for jointly-owned IP included in licensed subject matter, and our §2.1(a)–(c) licences cover Array's interests in the Joint Patents and Joint Know-How across Development, Manufacture and Commercialization in the whole Ono Territory. We therefore have a practical, field-wide right to exploit, so this is not the "joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit" walk-away.
2. **Termination assignments** of Product-specific Regulatory Filings and Trademarks (§§14.2(a)(iii), (vii)) are ordinary product reversion, with our corporate names carved out, and §14.2(a)(ix) requires Array to pay market-rate consideration where we terminate for its material breach or insolvency.
